newsitem.title: GERMANY: German retail coffee prices seen rising -KJS.
newsitem.headline: German retail coffee prices seen rising -KJS.

text.p: German retail prices of roasted coffee will rise to 12 marks per 500-gram packet from 10 marks as roasters' price hikes begin to bite, Kraft Jacobs Suchard (KJS) said on Monday.

KJS, part of Philip Morris, also said it would probably raise its own prices again in June. It made the general forecast, which it said applied broadly to all coffees across the German market, at a press briefing.
Market leader KJS said its ex-plant prices to the wholesale trade could rise 1.50 to 2.00 marks in June after an earlier round of rises in March.
Other roasters generally take KJS' lead but analysts said the market is competitive and can resist rises.
KJS spokesman Rolf Sauerbier said KJS would try and speed up the process of passing on increases in green coffees to the market in future.

Consumers should expect to be paying more than the psychological 10 marks level, perhaps until the summer of 1998. KJS' raw materials buyer Thomas Gehring said only then would coffee markets react negatively to increased supply from expanded Central American growing areas.
Arabicas should be tight at least until October 1997 because of unfavourable weather and area reductions, especially in Colombia, Germany's main supplier, Gehring said.
Price increases in the past have taken up to months to filter through in Germany, where supermarket chains often take deliberate losses in order to attract consumers.

KJS said it had not lost market share after raising ex-plant prices by 2.50 marks in March when high raw materials prices and dollar firmness first forced roasters to act. But average prices on German supermarket shelves have only risen by 0.50 marks.

KJS plans to publicise its intention to push through the increases to end-consumers at a number of briefings in major German cities this week. On Tuesday, it will brief the press in Hamburg. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
